title: Ops Daylight: Mini-roll cadence, cutover checklist, and release notes draft
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a lightweight, ops-facing plan for a series of mini-rolls ("minirolls") we want to run during daylight windows in early Oct 2026. Target: low-risk model/infra changes that need quick verification, plus one aggregated release note draft for product/marketing review. Focus is on minimal blast radius, fast rollback, and clear SRE/Product coordination.

Summary of changes in this wave (short):
- Serving runtime: kernel fallback improvement that avoids OOMs on long-sequence tails (v1.3.7 -> v1.3.8).
- Autoscaler: add a short quiesce window when draining nodes to avoid double-scaling oscillation.
- Console: per-route latency dashboard tweaks and a new rollout toggle for the Dedicated pool selector.
- Canary-only config: KV cache warmup flag enabled for 10% traffic on canary.

Quick decision matrix (what to do if we see X):
- 5-10% error spike sustained >5m: pause roll, scale canary down to 0, revert canary config (immediate rollback).
- Latency p95 increase >200ms vs baseline for 3 consecutive samples (5m cadence): pause and divert 100% of traffic to fallback model variant.
- Memory pressure above 85% on any node: immediate node quarantine, stop scheduler from placing new canary pods.
- Unexpected data path error (auth, routing): immediately cut canary traffic and escalate to Platform owner.

Preflight checklist (owners in parens) - run T-48h, then T-2h:
- Branch/PR merged and validated with integration tests (Ben).
- Canary config prepared and verified in staging (Lena).
- Baseline telemetry snapshot captured (last 72h): latency, error, throughput (Marco).
- Rollback artifacts baked: config patch + quick revert script (runbook snippet) (Aisha).
- Pager rotation for release window confirmed and on-call informed (SRE lead).
- Slack channel #release-ops pinned with links; Zoom bridge created (ops-call) (Priya).
- KMS keys and secret rotated checklist reviewed (security) if config touches keys (security reviewer).
- Post-release canary eval prompt set and eval harness defined (product/dex).

Mini-roll cadence: (planned windows)
- Day 1 (2026-10-05): Canary pilot - 1% global traffic -> check 60m -> 5% for 2h -> 10% for 1h. Decision: proceed to Next Day or rollback.
- Day 2 (2026-10-06): Gradual ramp if Day 1 green: 10% -> 25% over 3h -> 50% for 2h. If stable, leave 10% in canary while cutting release notes.
- Day 3 (2026-10-07): Controlled ramp to 100% for non-critical routes only (console toggle routes). Critical customer routes stay on pinned model.

Cutover step-by-step (minute-style for Day 1 pilot):
- T-minus 60 min: Final baseline snapshot; suspend scheduled heavy jobs; set higher sampling for traces (Marco).
- T-minus 30 min: Run smoke test suite against canary infra endpoint (Ben).
- T-minus 10 min: Announce on #release-ops and to on-call; confirm Zoom & runbook readiness (Aisha).
- T-zero: Flip header routing for 1% of eligible traffic (Lena) via rollout toggle.
- +5m: Verify canary instances healthy and KV cache warming running.
- +30m: Check p50/p95/p99, error rates, infra metrics (CPU, memory), and model outputs for sampling.
- +60m: Decision point: continue to 5% or rollback. Document decision and reasons.
- If continuing: perform 5% step, then observe for 2h. If rollback at any point: trigger revert script and redeploy prior canary config; notify all stakeholders.

Observability & signals to watch (owner):
- Latency heatmap by region and model variant (Marco).
- Error rate by HTTP code and by model-serving path (Ben).
- KV cache hit ratio and warmup success events (Lena).
- Autoscaler activity spikes and node drain durations (SRE).
- Rollout toggle state and API error traces (product).

Rollback triggers and procedure (quick):
- Trigger if any of the decision matrix conditions are met.
- Procedure: run revert script (ops/revert-canary.sh), scale canary pods to 0, route 100% back to baseline variant, remove new config flags, open rollback incident doc and tag the release.

Post-release verification (T+0 to T+72h):
- T+0–+2h: smoke suite on all regions; high-priority customer pings for known customers on pinned routes.
- T+4h: automated canary evaluation run against gold prompt sets; run Redwood Optimize quality checks.
- T+24h: full telemetry comparison vs baseline; prepare short incident log if any anomalies.
- T+72h: final sign-off or escalate to full incident review if >SLO breaches.

Release notes draft (product-facing bullets) - please review for tone and customer-facing wording:
- Runtime stability update: Improved kernel fallback behavior reduces memory-related failures for long-sequence requests, lowering error rates for large-context workloads. (engineering)
- Autoscaler refinement: Reduced oscillation during scale-down by introducing a short quiesce window, improving request routing stability during node transitions. (infra)
- Console UX: Added per-route Dedicated-pool toggle and clearer latency breakdowns in the route details page. Rolling out to 10% of accounts initially. (console)
- Internal: KV cache warmup opt-in for canary routes to pre-populate commonly used prefixes and reduce first-token latency for repeated prompts.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unseen model OOMs on extremely long tails. Mitigation: keep canary limited to non-critical routes + memory guardrails.
- Risk: Autoscaler interacts unexpectedly with cloud provider spin-up rates. Mitigation: SRE to monitor and hold manual approval for region-wide ramps.
- Risk: Console toggle might be exposed early. Mitigation: gate with feature-flag list and limit to internal accounts for first 24h.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Confirm which customer accounts are in the Dedicated pool test ring (Product to provide list).
- Add extra sampling of model outputs for semantic regressions (Product + Applied ML).
- Decide whether to include rollout in weekend maintenance window if Day 2 shows minor instability.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: merge PR + run end-to-end smoke (due T-24h).
- Lena: configure canary toggle and verify routing (due T-12h).
- Marco: capture baseline telemetry and enable 1s trace sampling (due T-48h).
- Priya: create release announcement draft and coordinate with comms (due T+0).
- Aisha: own rollback script and incident template; runbook updates (due T-48h).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: we keep critical customer routes pinned and only change console-only routes early. The goal is to validate kernel fallback and autoscaler quiescing without touching large production flows.
- Please add comments inline with any wording changes for the release notes; product will do final copyedit.

Appendix (quick links and commands):
- Revert script: repo ops/scripts/revert-canary.sh (run: bash revert-canary.sh --release-id=2026-10-miniroll)
- Smoke test: curl https://staging.canary-api.redwood-inference.internal/healthcheck
- Telemetry dashboard: Console > Rollouts > Miniroll-Oct-2026 > Telemetry

-- end --
